text:
maria: FYI ran a long nsys across the TRT-vLLM path after the kernel selector change — seeing a ~22% tail latency bump on p99 for short-chat workloads. attaching the top-level flame and a couple notes. :frowning:

devon: ugh. can you paste the command you used for the trace? was batching stable during the run?

maria: ran on a 3090 repro stack, mixed batch sizes (1,2,4), workload is short-seq chat. nsys command: ```nsys profile --trace=cuda,kernels,osrt --sample=none -o /tmp/trace_maria ./run_invoke.sh --model trt_vllm --concurrency 16```

sam: thanks. did you capture perfetto timeline too or just nsys? I want to see the host-side wrapper/scheduler timing vs kernel launch spikes.

maria: only nsys this round. I can repro with perfetto slice capture next. quick glance: most extra time is in host-side stalling between api->engine_invoke and kernel launch, and some kernel config path (an extra memcpy?)

liam: that might be the new kernel-picker fallback hitting for certain sequence lengths. if selector doesn't find a specialized kernel it falls back to a generic matmul kernel that calls cudamemcpy to reshape. did we change heuristics to prefer memory-safe kernels recently?

devon: yep we merged heuristics tweak in PR #2412 last week. It biases toward single-kernel-per-op to reduce context-switching, but maybe for short sequences it picks the wrong kernel.

maria: tracebot output (auto-summary): ```tracebot: summary: total GPU time 480ms, host wait 120ms, kernel config overhead 34ms, memcpy overhead 26ms, scheduler queue latency p95=18ms, p99=42ms```

sam: those memcpy numbers look suspicious for short sequences. could be kv cache handling — maybe we copy KV back/forth on every invoke for small batches. can you run a kv-instrumented trace? add env VAR to log kv cache hits/misses.

maria: plan: 1) repro with perfetto + nsys side-by-side; 2) run with KV_DEBUG=1 to log cache ops; 3) force kernel selector to previous policy and compare.

devon: for perfetto use: ```PERFETTO_SERVICE_ADDRESS=unix:/tmp/perfetto.socket perfetto -c perfetto_cfg.pb -o /tmp/trace.pb && traceconv /tmp/trace.pb /tmp/trace.html``` also add TRACING_FLAGS="slices,threads,processes" so we get wrapper slices.

liam: also try forcing batcher to use fixed batching (no dynamic merging) to isolate scheduler overhead: set REDWOOD_BATCHER_POLICY=fixed_8 or fixed_1 depending on traffic.

maria: running a 10-min sweep now with three variants: new-selector + dynamic batching, old-selector + dynamic, old-selector + fixed batching. will upload perfetto + nsys artifacts when done. ETA ~45m. :hourglass_flowing_sand:

sam: when you upload, include the small kernel-level nvprof snippet for single-invoke type: ```nvprof --print-gpu-trace --csv --profile-from-start off ./single_invoke_test``` we need per-kernel durations to see if the generic kernel is actually heavier.

tracebot: note: attaching quick diff from previous run: kernel_count increased by 12%, avg kernel launch overhead +0.9ms, scheduler wakeups +18%

devon: good call to check KV warmup. if cache miss rate increases for short prompts, that could explain memcpy+setup. maria add a run with KV_WARMUP=1 (prepopulate cache) to compare.

maria: I'll add KV_WARMUP and the forced selector flags. uploading first artifact now: /artifacts/1798765432/nsys_trace.zip. ping when you can review.

liam: grabbing it now. quick grep showed a repeated pattern: host thread does a serialize_config, then a cudamemcpy, then kernel launch(s), repeat. looks like selector inserted a micro-reshape path for batch=1 sequences.

sam: if reshape path is the issue we can try inline fast-path kernel for shape changes instead of memcopy — low-risk patch for a canary. or avoid selector fallback for sequences < 32 tokens.

maria: noted. I will run the canary patch that disables fallback for short sequences and re-run the 10-min sweep after lunch. thanks all. :thumbsup:

devon: awesome. if this reduces p99 by >10% we'll roll to canary on staging. keep the artifacts.

tracebot: reminder: please annotate the perf artifacts with commit hashes and config flags for future triage (automated tracking).
